Tutor Intelligence introduces the next generation of Cassie and Sonny

The company combines updated robot hardware and AI for case handling and individual-item picking in warehouses.

MassRobotics ↗16 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3Videos 3

Tutor Intelligence’s robots

MassRobotics shared news of Tutor Intelligence’s next-generation Cassie and Sonny, covering hardware, AI models and deployments. This Cassie is Tutor’s robot, not Agility Robotics’ biped of the same name.

Cassie gains mobility on the factory floor

Cassie is a single-arm robot on a wheeled base for case picking, depalletising and stacking. The company says the new version can travel between stations autonomously, has an integrated vacuum system and adds two 3D LiDAR units for environmental sensing.

Sonny targets individual-item picking

Sonny uses a form focused on human-like dexterity and is intended to use the 4.5-billion-parameter Ti0 vision-language-action model. Initial tasks include warehouse navigation, shelf picking and delivering orders to packing stations.

Business model and claims

Tutor offers usage-based pricing and says the new robots have already been deployed at US facilities. Claims about deployment speed and returns come from the developer and do not guarantee the same results at every warehouse.
